FINGERPRINT COMPARISON

On 22 September 2029 at 06.20 in Köpenick, a man’s body was found in the water near the jetty of Dahme Rowing Club; a hundred metres away, a capsized single racing scull.

The body was identified at the scene by his identical twin, Lukas Berger: Moritz Berger (27). He was wearing a club jacket embroidered “M. BERGER” on the chest.

Patrol note: “Moritz Berger was banned for two years for doping in 2028 and rowed alone at night. The club’s boatman saw him go down to the water alone at 22.00. The boat capsized in the dark; an accident.”

The two screws in the autopsy matched Lukas’s orthopaedic record; the survivor’s X-ray showed no screws. The fingerprint comparison tied the living twin to Moritz’s doping file.
An identification is itself a statement: look at who made it and what it rests on. What DNA cannot tell apart, the body and the records can.
Köpenick, Dahme Rowing Club — September 2029

For years Moritz Berger sold races and took money via Arendt; he was banned for doping. His identical twin Lukas was selected for the national team and decided to report his brother to the federation. On the night of 21 September Lukas went out on the water to prepare for selection; Moritz waited on the jetty, struck him with an oar on his return, swapped their jackets, left his brother in the water and turned the boat over. In the morning he identified the body bearing his own name and began living as Lukas.
